about.heading: About
paragraphs: I'm a Computer Science student at the University at Buffalo. I write software for robots that have to work outside a lab: navigation, SLAM, teleoperation, and control systems that fail safely instead of catastrophically.

Right now I'm doing research at DRONESLab, working on autonomy for quadruped robots. Before that, I worked on rovers for two robotics clubs at UB — leading autonomy for the NASA LunaBotics rover, and leading the whole project for the SpaceBulls rover.
about.looking: I finish my B.S. in December 2026, then I'm continuing at UB for an M.S. in Engineering Sciences (Robotics). I'm looking for a summer 2027 robotics internship — something in navigation, SLAM, or safety-critical control for robots that operate outside a lab.

projects.name: Fly MHW
projects.description: An experiment in designing a neural network that can play Monster Hunter World against multiple monsters using multiple weapons. It uses mixture-of-experts layers so it can generalize across monsters and weapons, with the goal of learning to fight a new monster as quickly as possible. I plan to train it with a combination of imitation learning and reinforcement learning.

captions.architecture.svg: The control loop: the network acts through a virtual gamepad, and a Lua mod reads the game's state back out. Dashed parts aren't built yet.
captions.gameplay.jpg: A recorded frame mid-hunt: the network observes exactly this pixel feed, nothing else — no privileged game state, per Design Principle 4.

projects.name: Go2 ROS 2 SDK
projects.description: My fork of the open-source ROS 2 SDK for Unitree's Go2 robot dog. It now runs directly on the robot's own onboard computer instead of needing a separate one, using a reproducible Nix setup. I tuned the navigation so the robot moves slowly and carefully, and fixed bugs in the lidar pipeline that were creating phantom obstacles, merging distinct map points together and wasting CPU. A staged smoke test checks every change before it runs on the real robot.

captions.01-go2.png: Onboard lidar point cloud in RViz, colored by height, with the Go2's model in the corridor it just mapped.
captions.02-supervisor-abort.png: Costmap replay of a run: the first plan (blue) against the actual track (green), stopping short of the goal footprint.

projects.name: VISION-Inspect
projects.description: VISION-Inspect is a DRONESLab project for autonomous culvert inspection. Rather than relying on a large labeled dataset of culvert defects, it leverages a vision-language model's generalization to navigate and inspect the culvert environment on its own, deciding what's worth a closer look instead of stopping to take pictures on a fixed schedule.

captions.01-culvert-inspection.jpg: Spot approaching a culvert to inspect, with a base station staged nearby for a network connection.

projects.name: Open-Spot: Spot Operator
projects.description: Spot Operator lets a person drive and control Boston Dynamics' Spot robot dog from a handheld Steam Deck. It's part of open-spot, DRONESLab's open-source toolkit for Spot, and it's the base the lab builds its research on. Normally Spot's lease — the token that says who's allowed to control it — is held by whatever laptop is driving it, so a dropped connection makes Spot sit down defensively. That's fine in a lab, but in the field, sitting down wherever it happens to be can be dangerous. Spot Operator instead runs a daemon on an onboard Jetson that holds the lease locally, so a dropped connection to the operator doesn't force the robot down. The emergency stop still always works.

captions.openspot-payload.webp: Modular sensor payload for Spot: Jetson enclosure, GPS antenna, IMU and long-range WiFi.

projects.name: NASA LunaBotics Rover
projects.description: UB's rover for NASA's LunaBotics competition, where university teams build robots that work on their own in simulated lunar terrain. I built its autonomy system, which lets the rover figure out where it is using its cameras, plan a path, and recover when it gets stuck, all without a driver. I led the autonomy subteam that took it from not working at all to ready for competition.

captions.img_3521.jpg: The rover driving through regolith simulant in the competition arena.
captions.img_3443.jpg: Staged before a run at the 2026 UCF Lunabotics competition.
captions.img_3499.jpg: Mission control: drive and drum controls, live camera feeds and telemetry over WebSockets.

projects.name: UB SpaceBulls Rover
projects.description: The rover built by UB SpaceBulls, the university's student robotics club. I worked on the software on its onboard hardware and built a simulated version of the rover in Gazebo, so the team could test changes on a computer before running them on the real robot. Along the way I went from leading one subteam to leading the whole project.

projects.name: Catan Agent
projects.description: Catan Agent is an AI that taught itself to play Settlers of Catan through trial and error, combining a graph neural network with reinforcement learning. It reads the board as a graph of connected tiles and settlements, so it can play on any board layout, not just the one it trained on. During training its opponents got tougher as it started winning more, which helped it improve faster.

captions.01-mean-return.png: Mean return over the fine-tuning run: the agent keeps gaining as its opponents get stronger.
captions.02-policy-entropy.png: Policy entropy falling as the agent commits to a strategy instead of exploring.
captions.03-losses-by-phase.png: Policy and value-function loss across all eight curriculum phases.
